title: Security in ASEAN delegates' hotel, Mendiola tightened amid protests
summary: Police on Wednesday tightened security along roads leading to Malacañang in Mendiola, Manila and around a hotel in Parañaque where foreign delegates to the ASEAN Summit 2026 stayed.

blocks.text: Police on Wednesday tightened security along roads leading to Malacañang in Mendiola, Manila and around a hotel in Parañaque where foreign delegates to the ASEAN Summit 2026 stayed.
Protesters continued to conduct activities against the visit of United States President Donald Trump in the Philippines.

In Manila, police set up barricades along Recto Avenue corner San Sebastian Street near Mendiola, blocking both lanes with barbed wire and three container vans, according to James Agustin's report on GMA News’ Unang Balita.
Legarda Street corner Figueras Street was also closed to motorists, while both lanes of Ayala Bridge were blocked, forcing motorists to take alternative routes.
Road closures affected commuters and transport workers. Some passengers had to walk after being dropped off near the barricades. Other motorists were also forced to take longer routes.
Police augmentation personnel from Police Regional Office 4A were positioned near Recto Avenue, while personnel from the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) were deployed around Mendiola.
The heightened security came as various groups continued holding protests against Trump's visit to the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit.
In Parañaque, police maintained heightened security around Solaire Resort Entertainment City, where various foreign ASEAN delegations stayed overnight, GMA News’ Bam Alegre also reported.

The Southern Police District monitored the area through advanced command posts at Solaire and the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), with police mobile units deployed at strategic locations.

Meanwhile, police continued to secure Liwasang Bonifacio as protesters including indigenous people concluded their three-day encampment, according to a report of GMA News’ Gabriel Gonzales on Unang Balita.
The Manila Police District (MPD) said 15 of the 22 people arrested in connection with protests since Sunday had already been charged.
Protesters had earlier attempted to proceed to Mendiola but police did not allow them to leave Liwasang Bonifacio.
The security measures are part of the interagency coordination following Trump's arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday for the ASEAN Summit 2026.

Trump is scheduled to go to Malacañang on Wednesday for a state visit with President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. The program includes arrival honors and a welcome ceremony at the Kalayaan Grounds at 11 a.m., followed by the signing of the guest book at 11:25 a.m. — Jamil Santos/RSJ, GMA News
